pageCache.pageTitle: Westside School | Outstanding Alternative Provision in West London
pageCache.text:
A School Built on Structure, Belief & High Expectations.
Westside exists for young people whose educational experience has not yet provided the conditions they need to thrive.
Many of our students arrive having experienced disruption in their previous settings. What they need is not reduced ambition, but an environment that is calm, predictable and purposeful, where adults remain consistent, and expectations stay high.
With small classes, strong relationships and a carefully structured school day, our students are able to rebuild confidence as learners while continuing to work towards meaningful academic outcomes.
Our aim is simple: to help young people rediscover the joy of learning, regain momentum in their education and leave with a clear direction and the confidence to shape their future.
The Westside Way
High expectations met with consistent, compassionate support
Personalised Learning Pathways
We take time to understand each student's unique experiences and needs, creating tailored learning plans that build on strengths and address challenges with care and intention.
Intentional Small Classes
With no more than eight students per group, every young person receives the individual attention they deserve. This creates a safe, supportive space where students can thrive.
Strong Pastoral Guidance
Our dedicated pastoral team works alongside students to rebuild self-esteem, develop resilience, and create positive momentum towards their futures.
Academic Pathways with Real Opportunities
Westside offers a broad and ambitious curriculum designed to prepare students for Post-16 pathways, including further education, training and employment.Students work towards recognised qualifications, prioritising GCSEs, while also developing practical skills, independence and resilience.Through personalised teaching and consistent support, students are able to rebuild confidence in their abilities and develop the knowledge and skills they need for the future.
Core subjects, such as English, Math, Science and option subjects
Vocational and practical learning opportunities
Personal development and enrichment
Preparation for further education, apprenticeships and employment
Referring to Westside School
High Expectations. Meaningful Outcomes.
Westside School has achieved two consecutive Ofsted Outstanding ratings, including under the new Ofsted framework.

pageCache.pageTitle: About Westside School | Structured Alternative Provision West London
pageCache.text:
A Different Kind of School
At Westside, we believe that every young person deserves the opportunity to succeed, regardless of the challenges they may have faced previously.‍Many students join Westside after experiencing challenges in mainstream education or periods of disruption to their learning. Often, behaviour reflects unmet needs rather than a lack of ability or potential.‍Our approach focuses first on understanding the individual student, including their experiences, strengths and challenges, before building the capacity needed to support them effectively.‍By providing structure, consistency and strong adult support, we help students regain stability in their education and begin to move forward again.
Our Vision
Our vision is to create a school environment where young people can:
Rebuild confidence in themselves and their abilities
Experience meaningful academic success
Develop resilience and independence
Prepare for further education, employment and adult life
We believe education has the power to transform lives, and we hold high expectations for every student who joins our school.
The Westside Way
At Westside, we believe in making the system work for the child, rather than expecting the child to adapt to a system that does not meet their needs.‍Before a student joins the school, we work closely with families, previous schools and external professionals to build a clear understanding of their circumstances and support requirements.‍This allows us to create a personalised learning plan, ensuring that students can continue their education while addressing any gaps in knowledge, confidence or engagement.
Our approach includes:
Small class sizes of no more than eight students
Highly qualified teaching staff
Strong pastoral support
Personalised learning pathways
Regular progress reviews and adjustments
This structure allows students to experience the stability and support they need to begin making meaningful progress.
Supporting the Whole Child
The Westside School Support
Education at Westside goes beyond academic learning.
Many of our students benefit from additional support to develop socially, emotionally and mentally. We work with a range of specialist professionals and interventions to ensure students receive the support they need to thrive.
Speech and Language Therapy
Occupational Therapy
Educational Psychology
Pastoral and well-being support
Alongside these services, students participate in enrichment activities and experiences that help build confidence, resilience and independence.
School Life at Westside
Life at Westside is designed to provide the structure, stability and support students need to rebuild confidence and re-engage with learning.Small class sizes and strong relationships with staff help create a calm, focused environment where students feel supported, challenged and able to make progress.Alongside academic learning, students take part in activities that support their personal development, confidence and well-being.
A consistent school day helps students build positive routines and maintain focus in their learning.Westside offers a range of enrichment activities that allow students to explore interests beyond the classroom while developing practical skills and confidence.Activities may include:• Performing arts• Cookery• Mentoring• Volunteering• Art and creative activities• Sports• E-sports• Community and outdoor experiences
A consistent school day helps students build positive routines and maintain focus in their learning.
Westside works closely with families, carers and professionals to ensure students receive consistent support both inside and outside the classroom.
Our Community
The Westside Community
A safe and supportive community is central to life at Westside.We work closely with families, carers and external professionals to ensure students receive consistent support both inside and outside the classroom.Our staff maintain an open and approachable culture where students feel able to ask for help, build trust and develop confidence.
Safeguarding
The safety and wellbeing of our students is our top priority.
If you have a safeguarding concern, please contact the school immediately so it can be addressed without delay.
Ofsted and Outcomes
Westside School has been judged Outstanding by Ofsted in two consecutive inspections, including under the new Ofsted framework.Inspectors recognised the school's strong culture of high expectations, consistent support and the significant progress many students make during their time at Westside.Students leave the school with recognised qualifications and go on to further education, training or apprenticeships, equipped with the confidence and skills needed for the next stage of their lives.
Leadership at Westside
Westside School is led by an experienced and committed leadership team, providing clear direction, strong oversight and a consistent focus on student outcomes.
Visit Westside
We are always happy to welcome visitors who would like to learn more about the school and our approach.

pageCache.pageTitle: Careers Education | Westside School CEIAG Programme
pageCache.text:
Preparing Students for ‍the Future
Careers Education, Information, Advice and Guidance (CEIAG) forms an important part of the curriculum at Westside.
Our programme is designed to help students:
Understand the world of work
Explore different career pathways
Develop employability skills
Make informed decisions about their next steps
Build confidence in their future ambitions
From Year 8 onwards, students begin to explore career opportunities and develop the skills they will need as they move towards post-16 education and employment.
Gatsby Benchmarks
Westside School’s careers programme follows the Gatsby Benchmarks, a nationally recognised framework for high-quality careers guidance.The eight Gatsby Benchmarks ensure that students receive structured and meaningful careers support throughout their time at school.These benchmarks include:
By following this framework, we ensure students receive the guidance and experiences needed to prepare for their future.
Work Experience and Employer Engagement
Experiencing the workplace helps students understand potential career pathways.
Westside works with employers and organisations to provide opportunities for students to engage with the world of work.
These opportunities may include:
Work experience placements
Employer talks and workshops
Industry visits and events
Networking opportunities with professionals
Through partnerships with organisations such as SPARK Charity and local employers, students gain valuable insight into different industries and career options.
Our Post-16 Pathways
As students approach the end of their time at Westside, we provide dedicated support to help them plan their next steps.Students receive guidance on a range of post-16 pathways, including:
Our careers team supports students through the application process, helping them identify the options that best match their interests, strengths and ambitions.
Westside is committed to supporting students even after they leave the school. Through the Westside Alumni Programme, former students can continue to receive guidance and support as they transition into further education and training. This ongoing connection helps ensure students remain supported as they take the next steps in their educational and professional journeys.
Careers Information for Students
Students are encouraged to explore different career pathways and consider the opportunities available to them.
Through careers lessons, guidance sessions and external resources, students can:
Explore different industries and professions
Understand the skills required for different careers
Research education and training pathways
Develop skills for job applications and interviews
Our careers team works closely with students to help them identify their interests and plan their future.
Careers Information for Parents and Carers
Parents and carers play an important role in supporting young people as they make decisions about their future.The careers section of the website provides resources to help families understand the options available after Year 11 and support their child in exploring potential career pathways.We encourage families to discuss future ambitions together and make use of the information and resources available.
Provider Access
Westside School complies with the Baker Clause, ensuring that students have access to information from a wide range of education and training providers.This allows students to learn about different technical qualifications, apprenticeships and training opportunities available after school.Providers interested in engaging with Westside students can contact the school to discuss opportunities to participate in our careers programme.

pageCache.pageTitle: Curriculum & Learning | Westside School in West London
pageCache.text:
Our Westside Curriculum Approach
At Westside, the curriculum is designed to balance academic progress, personal development and preparation for adulthood.‍Students follow a structured programme of learning that includes both core academic subjects and wider learning opportunities, allowing them to develop the knowledge and skills required for further education, training or employment.Our curriculum aims to help students:
Develop strong foundations in key subjects
Build confidence as learners
Understand the wider world and their place within it
Develop resilience, independence and self-belief
Prepare for future education and career pathways
Through consistent teaching and personalised support, students begin to see themselves as capable learners again.
Our Students Follow A Personalised Learning Pathway
Every student follows a unique journey based on their history and strengths.
Limited to a maximum of eight students for focused attention.
Calm environment with stronger staff relationships.
Small Classes, Strong Support
One of the defining features of education at Westside is our small class sizes.Classes are limited to a maximum of eight students, allowing teachers to provide focused attention and meaningful support for each individual.
Students benefit from:
More personalised teaching
Greater opportunity to ask questions and engage in lessons
Stronger relationships with staff
A calm and focused learning environment
This structure allows students to rebuild confidence and begin making consistent academic progress.
Westside School's Subjects and Qualifications
Students at Westside study a range of subjects that combine academic learning with practical and vocational opportunities.
Subjects offered include:
Mental Health Awareness
Many students work towards GCSE qualifications alongside vocational courses that help develop practical skills and career awareness.These qualifications ensure students leave Westside with recognised achievements that support their next steps.
STEM and Future Skills
Westside places strong importance on STEM education: science, technology, engineering and mathematics.‍Through STEM learning, students develop critical thinking, problem-solving and adaptability while exploring how these subjects connect to real-world opportunities.‍We also encourage all students, including girls who are historically underrepresented in STEM careers, to explore these pathways.
Progress and Achievement
Students at Westside develop not only academically, but also personally. Through a structured and supportive learning environment, students gain:
Confidence in their abilities
Improved engagement with learning
Stronger resilience and independence
A clearer understanding of their future goals
By the time students leave Westside, they are better prepared to continue their education and take the next steps towards adulthood.

pageCache.pageTitle: Safeguarding at Westside School | Report a Concern
pageCache.text:
Reporting a Safeguarding Concern
If a child is in immediate danger, please call 999 immediately.
You can also contact NSPCC Helpline on 0808 800 5000 for advice and support.
If you have a concern about the safety or well-being of a student at Westside School, please report it as soon as possible to our Designated Safeguarding Leads or through our safeguarding email: safeguarding@westsideschool.org.uk
Safeguarding Contacts
Safeguarding at Westside School is led by the following designated safeguarding staff:
safeguarding@westsideschool.org.uk
Our Approach
We take a proactive approach to safeguarding, creating a structured and supportive environment where students feel safe, respected and able to speak to trusted adults.Further information can be found in our Child Protection and Safeguarding Policy.
